text:
Predicates:
Engaged(x) ::: x is engaged.
Invite(x, y) ::: x invites y to their ceremony.
WeddingPlans(x) ::: x makes wedding plans.
WellAttendedWedding(x) ::: x has a well-attended wedding.
LargerFamily(x) ::: x has a larger family.
John ::: John.
Premises:
∀x (WeddingPlans(x) → Engaged(x)) ::: All people who make wedding plans are people who are engaged.
∀x (Invite(x, y) → WeddingPlans(x)) ::: All people who invite others to come to their ceremony make wedding plans.
∃x (WellAttendedWedding(x) ∧ Invite(x, y)) ::: Anyone who has a well-attended wedding invites others to come to their ceremony.
∃x (LargerFamily(x) ∧ (WellAttendedWedding(x) ∨ Invite(x, y))) ::: Some people that have well-attended weddings have larger families.
Engaged(John) → (¬Invite(John, y) ∧ WeddingPlans(John)) ::: If John is engaged, then John does not invite friends to their ceremony and makes wedding plans.
LargerFamily(John) → (WellAttendedWedding(John) ∨ Invite(John, y)) ::: If John has a larger family, then either John has a well-attended wedding or invites friends to their ceremony.
Conclusion:
John ::: John.
